stem: Which statement best distinguishes the mechanisms of H2-receptor antagonists and proton pump inhibitors (PPIs)?

options.A: Both drug classes inhibit the same gastric receptor and differ only in onset time.
options.B: H2-receptor antagonists block histamine H2 receptors on gastric parietal cells, whereas PPIs inhibit the gastric H+/K+ ATPase proton pump.
options.C: H2-receptor antagonists inhibit the gastric proton pump, whereas PPIs block histamine H2 receptors.
options.D: PPIs reduce acid secretion by blocking histamine H2 receptors on gastric parietal cells.

rationale: H2-receptor antagonists decrease gastric acid secretion by competitively blocking histamine H2 receptors on gastric parietal cells. PPIs act at a different target: the parietal-cell H+/K+ ATPase, the final proton pump in gastric acid secretion. Therefore, B is correct.
educational_objective: Differentiate H2-receptor antagonists from PPIs by their distinct targets in gastric acid secretion.

source_original.stem: A nurse is explaining the difference between an H2 receptor blocker (such as famotidine) and a proton pump inhibitor (such as omeprazole) to a client who assumes the two medications basically work the exact same way. The nurse should instead explain that:

options.A: H2 blockers and PPIs inhibit the same receptor and differ only in time to onset
options.B: H2 blockers block histamine H2 receptors while PPIs inhibit the gastric proton pump
options.C: H2 blockers provide more profound acid suppression than PPIs for erosive esophagitis
options.D: PPIs act mainly by blocking histamine H2 receptors on gastric parietal cells

source_original.rationale: H2 receptor blockers reduce gastric acid secretion by blocking histamine H2 receptors on stomach parietal cells, while PPIs work through a different, generally more potent and longer-lasting mechanism by directly and more completely inhibiting the proton pump (H+/K+ ATPase) responsible for acid secretion, making PPIs generally more effective for significant acid suppression.
source_original.source_detail: Mechanism section: PPIs inhibit gastric H+/K+ ATPase; contrasted with H2 receptor antagonists that block histamine H2 signaling; StatPearls; accessed 2026-08-14.
